issues.claim: legal_privacy: "Friedman v. Martinez (N.J. 2020) recognized intrusion upon seclusion for hidden cameras in restrooms/locker rooms and allowed claims by employees whose images were not provably captured."
issues.problem: Misstates the holding. The opinion (A-37/81-18, decided June 16, 2020) does hold that intrusion upon seclusion does not require proof that a plaintiff's image was actually recorded (circumstantial evidence suffices as a matter of law), but it then held that the record was insufficient for the Arendt plaintiffs - the women who could not identify themselves on the footage - and it REVERSED the Appellate Division, finding summary judgment for the defendants was properly granted. The brief states the opposite outcome for exactly those plaintiffs.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "Friedman v. Martinez (N.J. 2020) held that intrusion upon seclusion does not require proof that a plaintiff's image was actually recorded - circumstantial evidence can suffice - while affirming that on the 2014 record the plaintiffs who could not identify themselves on the footage had not met the summary-judgment standard (Appellate Division reversed). Cameras must never cover restrooms, locker rooms, changing areas or break rooms."

issues.claim: measured_outcomes (Ailytics): "the page states no outcome percentage"; caveats: "its logistics page states no outcome percentage at all"; data_gaps: "Ailytics' logistics/warehousing page as fetched did not contain the 60-80% non-compliance reduction ... so neither is asserted here"
